- `dependencyClosure` uses default `.sort()` (`offline-execution.ts:120`) while `exactSorted`/engine use `localeCompare` (`:101-103`; `engine.ts:178-180`, `:246-249`).

Impact: any plan whose selected ids include punctuation-ordered names can never pass closure validation — both creation and execution fail closed with no valid ordering.

### F6 — MEDIUM: `executionPolicy` is dropped during reproduction; non-default policies make a closure unusable

- `validateOfflineExecutionClosure` passes only `{ tasks, selectedTaskIds }` to `reproduceNormalizedPlan` (`offline-execution.ts:198-203`).
- `PlanDraftSchema.executionPolicy` defaults to the built-in policy (`engine.ts:33-37`), and `deriveBoundNormalizedPlan` hashes `draft.executionPolicy` into the plan digest (`:252-286`).

Impact: a legitimate non-default-policy plan can never be bundled/executed; offline execution silently uses engine defaults.

### F7 — MEDIUM: `ssh-keygen` is resolved from `PATH` for signing and signature verification

- `execute('ssh-keygen', …)` / `spawn('ssh-keygen', …)` (`offline-bundle.ts:15`, `:148`, `:169`).
- The sandbox, by contrast, pins `/usr/bin/bwrap` + `/usr/bin/readlink` and requires root ownership and non-writability (`offline-sandbox.ts:6-7`, `:52-54`, `:99-104`).

Impact: a `ssh-keygen` earlier on `PATH` can make both `verifySignature` and `verifyReleaseMembership` return success, collapsing the whole authenticity chain. PATH hijack implies broad compromise, but this is a weaker-than-necessary trust boundary for a verifier.

### F8 — MEDIUM/LOW: Zero-metadata bundles are signed with **no** closure validation, and verify/plan/apply accept them

- `createOfflineBundle` validates the closure only when at least one execution-metadata id exists (`offline-bundle.ts:381-391`). With **none**, it signs anyway (the existing base test does exactly this: `offline-bundle.test.mjs:71-76,84-110`).

Impact: `bundle-verify`/`bundle-plan` do not imply “execution closure.” A consumer keying approval off `manifest.planDigest` from a no-metadata bundle is trusting a caller-chosen digest that no plan artifact backs.

# Read-only adversarial audit — bounded concurrent TUI output retention

No files were edited. Findings verified against `packages/installer-engine/src/*.ts`, `dist/`, and the tests via read-only Node probes.

## Verdict

The **retention bound itself is sound**: per-task and global line/byte caps are enforced, byte accounting is exact, eviction is deterministic, and per-task attribution is preserved. The material problems are an **unbounded task-cardinality memory vector**, **sanitizer gaps for invisible/bidi/Unicode-separator text**, and a **cell-width model that under/over-counts keycap and ZWJ sequences**. Presentation defects are correctly isolated from execution.

## Findings

### F1 — MEDIUM: unbounded task map (memory + O(n²) growth)
`updateTask` (`renderers.ts:137-145`) creates a `TuiTaskView` for **any** incoming `taskId`. Eviction only ever removes *output lines*, never empty task entries (`renderers.ts:179-184` skips `outputSequences.length === 0` and `break`s). So:
- 6 000 distinct `taskId`s → 6 000 retained map entries (probe confirmed).
- 1 000 `task-status`-only events → 1 000 entries, zero output.
- 20 000-entry map → ~7.5 ms per subsequent append (each event copies the tasks map and scans all tasks at `renderers.ts:181-184`).

`retainedOutputBytes/Lines` correctly stay ≤1 MiB/2 048 (invariant held), so the **output** is bounded but the **model** is not. `reduceTuiEvent` is public (`index.ts:3`) and `onEvent` accepts a live stream (`renderers.ts:490-507`), so a buggy/compromised emitter grows heap without bound. Not covered by tests (fixtures cap at 2–20 tasks, `renderers.test.mjs:201-240`).

### F2 — MEDIUM (presentation integrity): sanitizer misses invisible / bidi / Unicode separators
`sanitizeTerminalText` (`renderers.ts:289-301`) escapes C0/C1 and ESC only. It passes through, confirmed by probe:
- U+2028 / U+2029 (line/paragraph separators) — terminals may render as **line breaks**, breaking the "one model line = one terminal row" invariant `renderTuiFrame` relies on (`renderers.ts:352-395`).
- U+200B (ZWSP), U+202E/U+202C (RTL override/terminate), U+2066-2069 (bidi isolates), U+FEFF (BOM) — enables Trojan-Source-style visual spoofing of task/output text.

ESC/OSC-52/CSI-2J/`\r`/`\n`/`\t` *are* neutralized (`renderers.ts:293-297`). This is a spoofing/row-corruption surface, not execution.

### F3 — LOW/MEDIUM (presentation): wrong terminal cell-width for keycap/ZWJ
`terminalCellWidth` (`renderers.ts:303-321`) counts keycap `1️⃣` as 1 cell (VS16→0, U+20E3 `\p{Mark}`→0) but terminals render 2 → `fitTerminalWidth` (`renderers.ts:323-336`) can emit lines **wider than `options.width`**. Conversely, ZWJ family `👨👩👧` counts 3×2=6 cells but renders 2 → over-truncation. The frame test `renderers.test.mjs:195-198` asserts **code-point count**, not cell width, so it cannot catch this (and is vacuous on the ASCII fixture).

### F4 — LOW: max-length Unicode lines silently vanish
A 16 384-char emoji or control line sanitizes to ≈65 544 bytes, exceeding `TUI_OUTPUT_BYTES_PER_TASK` (`renderers.ts:125,160-165`) → the **whole line is dropped** (probe: `keptLines 0`), not truncated. Accounting stays exact (`retainedOutputBytes 0`), but the operator loses the line entirely; the "N earlier output lines omitted" message (`renderers.ts:386-389`) conflates it with ordinary eviction.

### F5 — LOW: cross-task starvation (deterministic but unfair)
Global eviction (`renderers.ts:179-196`) is globally-oldest-first. A high-volume task continuously evicts the oldest lines held by *other* tasks, so one flooder can erase low-volume tasks' histories. Per-task cap (64 KiB) limits the flooder's own footprint but not this starvation. Deterministic and attributable; worth documenting.

### F6 — LOW: duplicate full-screen render on finish
`finish` for interactive TUI calls `writeTuiFrame()` **and** a manual `\u001b[H\u001b[J${renderTuiFrame(...)}` (`renderers.ts:519-522`) → two full redraws (flicker). `renderTuiFrame` also re-resolves options with `process.env` (`renderers.ts:352-353`) rather than the session-resolved options.

### F7 — LOW: diverging env semantics
`projectInstallerEvent` calls `resolveRendererProjectionOptions(optionsInput, {})` — an **empty** environment (`renderers.ts:399`), while `renderTuiFrame` uses `process.env` (`:353`). Inert today (plain projection never colors) but a latent inconsistency.

### F8 — LOW: spill log silently disabled for long run IDs
CLI composes `runId = ${input.runId}.${randomUUID()}` (`cli.ts:270`) → up to 165 chars, but `runIdentifier` caps at 128 (`renderer-spill-log.ts:5`). Probe: a 137-char composed id throws `ZodError`; the error is stored (`cli.ts:271`) and re-thrown on the first backpressure spill (`cli.ts:284`), which `renderers.ts:435-438` converts to drop + close. Result: spill evidence is silently lost for `input.runId > 91` chars.

## Verified correct (adversarial checks that passed)
- **Exact accounting**: `retainedOutputBytes == Σ Buffer.byteLength(sanitized line)` and `retainedOutputLines == Σ output.length` held under mixed ASCII/CJK/combining/emoji/control and 6 000 tasks; `retained + dropped == appended` (`renderers.ts:147-199`).
- **Boundary semantics**: caps use `>` (equal allowed); a single append cannot exceed the 1 MiB global (max line ≈64 KiB); per-task byte cap verified to 64 256 B ≤ 65 536 B (`renderers.ts:124-128,160-165`).
- **Deterministic eviction**: `sequence` is globally unique/strictly increasing, so the oldest-first comparison (`renderers.ts:183-184`) has no ties; identical streams produce identical retained output.
- **Attribution**: stream prefix at `renderers.ts:219`; lock/status keyed by `taskId` (`:207-218`); inspection reads only the selected task (`:376-391`); test `renderers.test.mjs:224`.
- **Presentation cannot affect execution**: every sink/parse/`finish` path is wrapped and localized to `closed`/`detached`/`failureCount` (`renderers.ts:440-450,470-489,490-507,508-525`); sibling sessions unaffected (test `:98-110`); terminal input isolation at `terminal-controller.ts:77-79,113-126`. `presentRun` never lets a renderer throw into `execute`.
- **Bounded spill**: byte/chunk limit checked **before** write, no partial chunk (`renderers.ts:429-439`); `spilledBytes` matches emitted bytes (test `:112-126`); spill-log append is exact and O_EXCL/fd-inode/nlink/mode verified (`renderer-spill-log.ts:52-74,90-95,110-123`).

## Test-coverage gaps
`renderers.test.mjs` has no coverage for: task-map cardinality, per-task **byte** cap, exact-byte equality (only `<=` at `:218,236`), bidi/zero-width/U+2028, keycap/ZWJ cell width (only code points at `:197`), and fair cross-task retention. It also never exercises the long-runId spill path (`cli.ts:270`). The `renderInstallerResult` batch path (`renderers.ts:536-548`) never uses the TuiModel, so the bounded-retention logic applies **only** to the interactive session — confirmed by reading, worth documenting.
